source.title: Role of Momentum in Smoothing Objective Function in Implicit Graduated Optimization

record.file_problem: The supplied paper text appears complete, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: It measures test accuracy for SGD, SHB and NSHB across batch sizes on CIFAR100, addressing whether batch size and momentum affect generalization. This is a different empirical setup from the cited large-batch studies and does not test random-label memorization or the other mapped versions.
record.gate_note: Rows report the paper's own CIFAR100 test-accuracy comparisons and explicitly described results. Theoretical smoothing formulas, estimated critical batch sizes, and cited findings are not separate behavioral results for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures its own held-out accuracy across batch sizes under a fixed 200-epoch budget on CIFAR100, directly testing V5 in two architectures with SGD, SHB and NSHB. It is a new setting using batch-size comparisons, rather than a different measurement method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors attribute momentum's generalization and batch-size robustness to greater objective smoothing, whose proposed degree depends on learning rate, batch size, momentum, gradient variance and a gradient-norm bound. They also conclude that their implicit graduated optimization schedules outperform constant-parameter momentum training. These are the authors' interpretations; the accuracy experiments do not directly establish the proposed smoothing mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares SGD, stochastic heavy ball (SHB), and NSHB on CIFAR100 test accuracy over batch sizes and proposes schedules based on its smoothing analysis. The mapped large-batch studies and recipes are not reproduced directly.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with optimizer, architecture and batch size; under a fixed 200-epoch budget, the largest batches show declines for SHB.

fits_no_version.finding: The measured SFO-minimizing batch sizes for ResNet18 are 512 for SGD, 1024 for SHB and 512 for NSHB.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Momentum formulation affects the batch size that minimizes training oracle complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that smoothing-reduction schedules improve ResNet18 test accuracy and training loss over constant-parameter SHB; analogous WideResNet results appear in Figure 17 without separately readable values here.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Schedules motivated by implicit graduated optimization can improve performance over constant-parameter momentum training.

record.problems: The reported accuracy comparisons use CIFAR100 and a fixed 200 epochs; the authors caution that update steps may be insufficient for the largest batches. Accuracy results are mostly shown in plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The paper's broad explanation that smoothing improves generalizability is argued theoretically and with these experiments, but the paper does not measure the training-test gap directly.

Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.

Language models; longer training as a remedy; learning-rate scaling with warmup; normalization or regularization remedies. The scheduling experiments do not establish recovery relative to a matched small-batch baseline.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, measured generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. No challenges verdict is warranted: SGD's deterioration agrees with V5, while SHB's stable ranges qualify batch sensitivity and its largest-batch deterioration supports the fixed-budget penalty. The supplied text omits readable plot curves, so separate NSHB outcomes cannot be recovered. No numerical accuracy differences or uncertainty estimates are stated.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test-error behavior when width exceeds the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language models; the study compares optimizers over batch sizes for 200 epochs on CIFAR100, not the full range of workload-dependent batch-size effects or adapted recipes described in the version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Trained across batch sizes for 200 epochs; measured test accuracy.
rows.value: Test accuracy deteriorated as batch size increased.
rows.note: Compared with SHB and NSHB; the text describes worsening test accuracy as batch size rises.
rows.check: Deteriorating accuracy with increasing batch size agrees with V5; the extracted state and challenges verdict have the direction backward. Batch sizes are 2^3–2^13 (8–8192), not 23–213. The relevant baseline is SGD at smaller batches. Learning rate was fixed at 0.1.

rows.subject: SHB
rows.operation_detail: Trained across batch sizes for 200 epochs; measured test accuracy.
rows.baseline: SGD test accuracy across batch sizes
rows.value: Test accuracy remained stable as batch size increased; best and roughly the same test accuracy for batch sizes of 28 to 212.
rows.note: Accuracy decreased at very large batch sizes 213, despite similar stated smoothing; the authors note larger batches may have had insufficient update steps.
rows.check: This row combines distinct conditions: the batch-size penalty is absent over 2^8–2^12 (256–4096), but observed at 2^13 (8192). Split these conditions for precise states. Compare SHB with smaller-batch SHB, rather than using SGD as the batch-effect baseline. Learning rate was 0.1 and momentum 0.9.

rows.subject: NSHB
rows.operation_detail: Trained across batch sizes for 200 epochs; measured test accuracy.
rows.baseline: SGD test accuracy across batch sizes
rows.value: The paper reports SHB generalizability remained stable; it does not separately state NSHB's accuracy trend in prose.
rows.note: The plotted NSHB values are not described separately in text, so a precise direction or value cannot be assigned.
rows.check: The supplied figure text contains no readable NSHB curve values, and the prose does not establish its separate accuracy trend. Batch sizes are 2^3–2^13 (8–8192). The relevant baseline is smaller-batch NSHB.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Trained across batch sizes for 200 epochs; measured test accuracy.
rows.value: Test accuracy worsened as batch size increased.
rows.note: Authors state this trend occurred for both ResNet18 and WideResNet-28-10.
rows.check: Worsening accuracy with increasing batch size supports V5, rather than reversing it. Batch sizes are 2^2–2^11 (4–2048). The relevant baseline is smaller-batch SGD. Learning rate was 0.1.

rows.subject: SHB
rows.operation_detail: Trained across batch sizes for 200 epochs; measured test accuracy.
rows.baseline: SGD test accuracy across batch sizes
rows.value: Test accuracy remained stable as batch size increased; almost equal test accuracy from batch sizes of 24 to 29.
rows.note: Accuracy decreased at very large batch sizes 210 and 211; authors say the number of steps may have been insufficient.
rows.check: Split the stable range, 2^4–2^9 (16–512), where the penalty is absent, from 2^10 and 2^11 (1024 and 2048), where accuracy decreases and the penalty is observed. The relevant baseline is smaller-batch SHB. Learning rate was 0.1 and momentum 0.9.

rows.subject: ResNet18 trained with SHB, Algorithm 3
rows.operation_detail: Compared constant hyperparameters with schedules that reduce degree of smoothing; measured test accuracy and training loss.
rows.baseline: SHB with constant learning rate, batch size, and momentum
rows.value: The paper states the noise-reduction method outperformed constant-parameter SHB on both test accuracy and training loss.
rows.note: The paper does not provide numeric values in text; this is its proposed schedule, outside the claim versions' specified interventions.
rows.check: This is a proposed scheduling-method comparison, without a matched large-versus-small-batch penalty or recovery comparison. Section 4.3 describes noise-reduction methods collectively; it does not restrict the stated improvement to simultaneous learning-rate and momentum decay. It should not be a claim-evidence row.

rows.subject: WideResNet-28-10 trained with SHB, Algorithm 3
rows.operation_detail: Compared constant hyperparameters with schedules that reduce degree of smoothing; measured test accuracy and training loss.
rows.baseline: SHB with constant learning rate, batch size, and momentum
rows.value: Figure 17 plots test accuracy and training loss for the proposed method; no textual result description is given.
rows.note: This is the paper's own algorithm comparison, not a test of a mapped version.
rows.check: This proposed scheduling-method comparison does not isolate a V5 batch-size penalty or its recovery. Figure 17 contains several scheduling variants, not only simultaneous learning-rate and momentum decay. It should not be a claim-evidence row.

relationships.condition: SGD on CIFAR100 with ResNet18 and WideResNet-28-10, fixed learning rate 0.1 and 200 epochs
relationships.reason: The authors explicitly report worsening test accuracy as batch size increases for both architectures; R1 and R4.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports worsening test accuracy with increasing SGD batch size for both architectures, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: SHB with learning rate 0.1 and momentum 0.9: ResNet18 batches 256–4096 and WideResNet-28-10 batches 16–512, 200 epochs
relationships.reason: Accuracy remains approximately equal across these ranges, showing that batch sensitivity depends on optimizer and workload; R2 and R5.
relationships.display_finding: Approximately equal accuracy across the specified batch ranges was reported for both architectures, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: SHB at the largest tested batches: ResNet18 batch 8192 and WideResNet-28-10 batches 1024 and 2048, 200 epochs
relationships.reason: Accuracy decreases beyond the stable ranges; the authors identify insufficient update steps as a possible explanation under the fixed epoch budget; R2 and R5.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports accuracy declines beyond stable SHB batch ranges, but these comparisons remain unverified and insufficient updates are only a proposed explanation.
